John 20:23 links Spirit-gift, sending, forgiveness, and retention; ecclesial, communal, declarative, disciplinary, and sacramental readings differ, and none licenses coercion or concealment of crime.
John 21 functions as an epilogue after the purpose statement in 20:30-31; whether it was composed later or by another hand is disputed.
The continuous Greek Gospel is internally anonymous; neither its narrator nor its purpose statement supplies the author's personal name.
The beloved disciple is presented as an authoritative witness, yet the Gospel never names that figure John son of Zebedee and John 21:24 speaks of the disciple in the third person.

John 20:31 states that selected signs are written for belief and life; manuscripts vary between forms often translated 'may believe' and 'may continue believing,' but the aspect alone does not securely identify evangelistic or confirmatory audience purpose.

John 20 narrates Mary Magdalene's encounter and commission, appearances to gathered disciples, and Thomas's confession; the episodes hold testimony, recognition, embodied wounds, Spirit, peace, and belief together.
Signs-source, discourse-source, displacement, multiple-edition, and Johannine-school models attempt to explain seams and development, but no proposed source or edition survives independently.
